rate.text: A southern city's only big club. Fanatical crowd. Won two league titles in recent years. A flamboyant film-producer owner.
A shipbuilding city's club that drew 40,000 even in the third tier. A documentary followed its fall. A young side just won promotion back to the top.
A one-city giant owned by the investment arm of your NFL team. A fierce, sometimes hostile crowd. Up and down between divisions.
The loudest stadium in its country; once won Europe's top prize. Owned by a former owner of your baseball team's biggest rival. Regular fan clashes.
A big-city club controlled by a private-equity firm. Spent over a billion on young players on very long contracts. Loud in patches.
A coastal club with a famously loyal crowd, a steady stream of academy players and left-leaning ultras. The coach came up through its youth teams.
The most successful club in its country, owned by an industrial dynasty. Tied to a match-fixing scandal and a breakaway league. Quiet modern stadium.
Founded by an electronics company for its workers. Wins its league often. Modern but loud ground. Sells its best players every year.
Started by supporters as an amateur team in 2012. Plays in a restored high-school stadium with a raucous, left-leaning supporters' group. Now pro in the second tier.
A mission-driven club founded in 2018 near you. Artists and activists among the owners. Struggling on the field; plays in a borrowed ballpark.
A member-owned capital-city club whose academy produced world stars. Won its league recently with a young coach. Ultras groups with a violent past.
A small club two hours from you, founded in 2021. A small seaside stadium. Mostly losing seasons so far.
Owned by a Gulf royal family's state group. Won almost everything for a decade. Charged with over 100 breaches of finance rules.
